title: First and Second Declension Adjectives
subtitle: bonus, bona, bonum. Agreement in case, number, gender.
objectives: Decline first/second declension adjectives in all genders.
Apply the rule of agreement: adjectives match their nouns in case, number, and gender.
Translate sentences with adjectives modifying nouns.
Recognize that adjectives do not need to match nouns in declension, only in case/number/gender.

sections.heading: Adjectives and agreement
sections.body:
Latin adjectives change their endings to match the nouns they modify. An adjective must agree with its noun in three ways: case, number, and gender. The adjective does not need to belong to the same declension as the noun.

The model adjective bonus (good) declines like a second-declension masculine noun in the masculine, a first-declension noun in the feminine, and a second-declension neuter in the neuter:

          Masc.    Fem.     Neut.
  Nom.    bonus    bona     bonum
  Gen.    bonī     bonae    bonī
  Dat.    bonō     bonae    bonō
  Acc.    bonum    bonam    bonum
  Abl.    bonō     bonā     bonō

Examples:
  vir bonus — a good man (masc. nom. sg.)
  puella bona — a good girl (fem. nom. sg.)
  templum bonum — a good temple (neut. nom. sg.)
  virī bonī — good men (masc. nom. pl.)
  puellam bonam — a good girl (fem. acc. sg.)

sections.heading: Examples from Cicero and Caesar
sections.body:
Cicero writes: vir bonus. — A good man.

Caesar writes: oppidum magnum. — A large town.

Vergil writes: arma virumque. — Arms and the man. (no adjective, but 'virum' is accusative singular masculine to agree with 'arma' in a compound object).
